messages:
Alex K: Quick idea — our embeddings SLO sampling window is currently 5m and it's giving noisy p50/p95 during bursty workloads. Thinking we should try a sliding 15m window with an exponential decay (give more weight to recent traces) and surface an 'SLO window' toggle in the console so tenants can pick 5/15/60m. Thoughts?
Maria P: Agree we need something less jumpy. 5m reacts too fast to single large batched requests, especially when dim-mixed jobs spike. 15m seems reasonable as a default.
Sam H: What about telemetry cardinality? If we expose window per-tenant it'll increase saved metrics. Can we compute SLO on the rollup side and only emit windows for tenants with >X qps?
Luis G: Good point. We could keep the high-cardinality time-series internal and only show the tenant-level aggregated SLO metric in the console. Backend computed, frontend reads single timeseries per-tenant.
Priya R: Also need to consider how batching and mixed-dims affect the observed latency. Large batches artificially inflate p95 even though per-request latency is fine. We should add an annotation when the window contains >N% requests that were split by the splitter (mixed dims / chunking).
Alex K: I like the annotation idea. UX should clarify 'what influenced this SLO' — split/merge events, fallback models, cross-region routing. :bulb:
Maria P: For sampling, do we rely on 100% spans or a probabilistic sampler? Current tracing is 1% and is missing small-tenants entirely. Maybe for SLO compute we need deterministic sampling for latency metrics (e.g., sample first K requests per minute per tenant).
Sam H: Deterministic per-tenant head sampling is cheap. Could do "first 10 reqs/min per tenant" and fall back to probabilistic for high qps tenants. That gives coverage for low-volume customers.
Luis G: Implementation detail: runtime collects per-request labels (tenant, dims, batch_size, splitter_action). We already tag splitter_action but not persisted to the metric pipeline. Need to add that tag and a tiny extra payload. Ops cost: small increase in metrics cardinality.
Priya R: For quota interactions — if tenant hits soft quota and we start dropping or splitting, SLO window should mark those periods. Otherwise we punish them for expected degradation. The console should show a shaded region for quota-limited intervals.
Alex K: Agreed. Also adding a routing-policy dimension: if requests got routed to a lower-cost fallback model, annotate that too. That helps correlate cost/quality tradeoffs.
infra-bot: Deploy queued: feature/emb-slo-window -> staging (sha: 7a1f3b)
Maria P: Can we get a small PoC: 15m sliding, decay alpha=0.2, deterministic head-sample 10/min, annotate splitter/fallback/quota? If staging looks good we'll try canary on 10% tenants.
Sam H: I'll sketch the telemetry changes and a minimal Grafana panel. Then we can add a console toggle.
Alex K: Perfect. Action items: Sam -> telemetry PR with sampler + tags; Luis -> ensure splitter_action exported; Priya -> console UX for toggle + shaded quota regions; Maria -> staging canary plan. I'll coordinate rollout. :thumbsup:
Maria P: sounds good. One more ask — add an automated regression alert when p95 deviates >30% vs a 7d baseline (after change) so we can roll back quickly.
Alex K: Yup we will. Thanks team.
